facts.text: Founded in 1867 by the Union Pacific, Sidney was named after railroad attorney Sidney Dillon, who helped steer the transcontinental line.
The town grew around Fort Sidney, a military outpost whose primary job was protecting Union Pacific track layers from hostile Native American attacks.
Once dubbed “the toughest town on the tracks,” Sidney attracted Western legends like Wild Bill Hickok, Calamity Jane, and Buffalo Bill Cody.
In 1949, the first successful oil well north of Sidney was drilled, adding oil to the local economy and reshaping the region.
The former headquarters of Cabela’s sat in Sidney until 2017, when the company was acquired by Bass Pro Shops and the building was repurposed.
